learning_outcomes.text: Understand and know the scientific and mathematical principles of machine theory.
Adequately know machine theory, including some cutting-edge knowledge in its field.
Be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate, and solve problems in machine theory using established methods.
Be able to choose and apply relevant analytical and modeling methods in the analysis and calculation of machines.
Be able to apply their knowledge to develop and carry out mechanical designs that meet specific requirements.
Have an understanding of the different methods for analyzing machines and components and the ability to use them.
Be able to combine theory and practice to solve problems in machine science.
Have an understanding of applicable methods and techniques in machines and their limitations.
Function effectively both individually and as part of a team.
A systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects of their branch of engineering.
Adequate knowledge of their branch of engineering, including some cutting-edge knowledge in its field.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate, and solve engineering problems using established methods.
The ability to choose and apply relevant analytical and modeling methods.
The ability to apply their knowledge to develop and carry out designs that meet specific requirements.
Understanding of different methods and the ability to use them.
The ability to design and conduct experiments, interpret data, and draw conclusions.
Technical and laboratory competences.
The ability to select and use appropriate equipment, tools, and methods.
The ability to combine theory and practice to solve engineering problems.
The understanding of applicable methods and techniques and their limitations.
Function effectively both individually and as part of a team.
Demonstrate awareness of the responsibility of engineering practice, social and environmental impact, and commitment to professional ethics, responsibility, and standards of engineering practice.

That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, although supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, abilities and skills in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to design a system, component or process in the field of mechanical engineering to meet required specifications.
Knowledge and ability to apply computational and experimental tools for the analysis and quantification of mechanical engineering problems.
Ability to design and conduct experiments and to analyze and interpret the data obtained.
Knowledge of the principles of theory of machines and mechanisms.

syllabus_topics: Introduction. Fundamental mechanisms. Passive resistances. Bearings.
Shocks and impacts in kinematic pairs.
Hypoid gears. Analysis of stresses in gears.
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the assessment consists of 40% continuous assessment (10% practices + 30% continuous assessment tests) and 60% final exam. For the extraordinary call, students can choose between this same distribution or a 100% final exam. Attendance at practices is mandatory, and they must be passed. A minimum grade of 4 out of 10 on the final exam is required to pass the course in both ordinary and extraordinary calls.
